lessons.title: Close-up: beard, neck, wreath and eyes

zoom.label: His chin and jaw, below the smiling mouth

c1.text: Level one: a smiling young rider with a short beard. Now zoom to his chin.

zoom.label: His chin and jaw, below the smiling mouth

c1q.text: What is his beard made of?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record Ma 3104 (MNC 2128), 'Tête du cavalier Rampin' (our translations)

c1a.text: Look closer: it is all bumps.

correction.tempting: From afar the beard looks like one shape.
correction.truth: It is carved as rows of tiny beads.
correction.evidence: The crop; the Louvre record lists a beard.

c1b.text: Yes. Each tuft is a little bead of marble, set in rows. The sculptor turned hair into pattern.

correction.tempting: Beards are often carved in waves.
correction.truth: His beard is short, carved as rows of beads.
correction.evidence: The crop; the Louvre record lists a beard.

c1m.text: A beard of beads, one by one.

zoom.label: The base of his neck and the top of his chest

c2.text: Level one: his body is in Athens. Now zoom to where head meets chest.

zoom.label: The base of his neck and the top of his chest

c2q.text: What is the line at the base of his neck?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record Ma 3104 (MNC 2128), 'Tête du cavalier Rampin' (our translations)
Acropolis Museum, Athens, collection record Acr. 590, 'Statue of a rider. The "Rampin Rider"'

c2a.text: No jewellery: it is a join.

correction.truth: It is where the original head meets the plaster cast.
correction.evidence: The Louvre record; the Acropolis Museum.

c2b.text: It is a join, on purpose.

correction.truth: The head is original and the body is a cast; this is where they meet.
correction.evidence: The Louvre record; the Acropolis Museum.

c2c.text: Yes. Above the line is the ancient marble head; below it is the Louvre's cast of the body in Athens.

zoom.label: The top of his head, above the curls

c3.text: Level one: his wreath most probably marks a victory. Now zoom to the top of his head.

zoom.label: The top of his head, above the curls

c3q.text: What is his wreath made of?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record Ma 3104 (MNC 2128), 'Tête du cavalier Rampin' (our translations)
Acropolis Museum, Athens, collection record Acr. 590, 'Statue of a rider. The "Rampin Rider"'

c3a.text: Yes: leaves, carved over the curls. The Louvre calls them oak; the Acropolis Museum says wild celery or oak.

correction.tempting: It hugs the head like a band.
correction.truth: It is a wreath of leaves carved over the hair.
correction.evidence: The Louvre record; the Acropolis Museum.

c3c.text: Look: it is made of little leaves.

correction.tempting: It runs round like a headband.
correction.truth: It is a wreath of leaves.
correction.evidence: The Louvre record; the Acropolis Museum.

c3m.text: Leaves, not metal: a winner's wreath.

zoom.label: His eyes, his ear and the curls beside it

c4.text: Level one: traces of red paint survive on him. Now zoom to his eyes and hair.

zoom.label: His eyes, his ear and the curls beside it

c4q.text: Where can you still see red?

sources.title: Musée du Louvre, collection record Ma 3104 (MNC 2128), 'Tête du cavalier Rampin' (our translations)
Acropolis Museum, Athens, collection record Acr. 590, 'Statue of a rider. The "Rampin Rider"'

c4a.text: The traces are in the hair, eyes and beard.

correction.tempting: Lips are the part we expect to be red.
correction.truth: Red survives on the hair, irises and beard.
correction.evidence: The Louvre record; the Acropolis Museum.

c4b.text: Yes. The Louvre records red in his hair, irises and beard; the Acropolis Museum notes colour on his face and hair.

correction.truth: Red traces survive on the hair, irises and beard.
correction.evidence: The Louvre record; the Acropolis Museum.

extends.concept: From 'a short beard' (level) to how it is carved: rows of tiny beads

c1q.what_you_learn: His short beard is carved as rows of tiny beads of marble.
